chief_complaint: pain and swelling in the right ankle after tripping on stairs
hpi_details: tripped while walking down the stairs this morning. The right ankle inverted (the sole turned inward). Noticed immediate pain and swelling on the outer side of the ankle. Can put weight on it and take a few steps, but it is quite painful to walk. No previous ankle injuries.
ideas: thinks it is a sprain but is not sure
concerns: worried that it might be fractured or broken
expectations: wants to know if he needs to go to the hospital for an X-ray and how to reduce the swelling

Assess weight-bearing ability and bony tenderness as part of the Ottawa ankle rules

suggested_questions: How exactly did you hurt your ankle?
Did you hear a pop or a snap when it happened?
Are you able to put weight on your foot and walk a few steps?
Where exactly does it hurt the most? Is the bone at either ankle bump tender?
Have you had any injuries to this ankle before?
What have you done so far to help the pain?

objective_cues.objective: Practise history-taking for an acute joint injury (mechanism of injury, weight-bearing ability)
objective_cues.say: How exactly did you hurt it, and can you put weight on it?

objective_cues.objective: Assess weight-bearing ability and bony tenderness as part of the Ottawa ankle rules
objective_cues.say: Can you take four steps, and is either ankle bone very tender to touch?

objective_cues.objective: Explain short-term protection, ice, compression, and elevation for comfort and swelling
objective_cues.say: Protect it, use ice and a comfortable wrap, and raise it when resting; start gentle movement as pain allows.

objective_cues.objective: Practise empathetic listening and setting expectations for healing times
objective_cues.say: Recovery varies with the severity; many sprains improve over a few weeks, but worsening pain or inability to bear weight needs reassessment.
